title: Longest Arithmetic Subsequence of Given Difference
statement: You get an integer array `arr` and an integer `difference`. Choose a subsequence of `arr` (drop any number of elements, possibly none, and keep the rest in their original order) in which each element minus the one before it is exactly `difference`. Return the largest possible length of such a subsequence. A single element always qualifies, so the answer is at least 1.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every pair `j < i` to see whether `arr[i]` can extend a chain ending at `arr[j]` works but costs O(n²). The difference is fixed, though, so the only element that can come right before `value` is `value - difference`. If we remember, for each value, the longest valid chain that ends with it among the elements seen so far, one hash lookup gives the best chain to extend.

## Approach

1. Keep a map `dp` from a value to the length of the longest valid subsequence ending in that value so far, and `best` for the overall maximum.
2. Scan `arr` from left to right. For each `value`, look up `previous = dp[value - difference]` (0 if absent).
3. The longest chain ending at this `value` has `length = previous + 1`; store it in `dp[value]`. A later copy of the same value always does at least as well as an earlier one, so overwriting is safe.
4. Update `best` and return it after the scan.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr = [1, 2, 3, 4]`, `difference = 1`.

- `1`: `dp[0]` is missing, so `length = 1`; `dp = {1: 1}`.
- `2`: `dp[1] = 1`, so `length = 2`; `dp[2] = 2`.
- `3`: `dp[2] = 2`, so `length = 3`.
- `4`: `dp[3] = 3`, so `length = 4`, and `best = 4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one map lookup and one update per element.
- Space: O(n) for the map in the worst case (all values distinct).

## Pitfalls

- Read `dp[value - difference]` **before** writing `dp[value]`; with `difference = 0` they are the same key, and the order makes the chain count repeated values correctly.
- The predecessor is `value - difference`, not `value + difference`; a negative difference makes the chain decrease.
- Order matters: a matching value that appears later in `arr` cannot come before the current one, which the left-to-right scan handles automatically.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `dp` | value → longest valid subsequence ending with that value so far |
| `best` | longest length found overall |
| `value` | the current element of `arr` |
| `previous` | length of the chain ending at `value - difference` (0 if none) |
| `length` | length of the best chain ending at the current element |

narration.2: dp maps a value to the longest valid subsequence seen so far that ends with that value.
narration.3: best tracks the longest such subsequence anywhere.
narration.5: Scan left to right so every chain only uses earlier elements.
narration.6: The only possible predecessor of value is value - difference; take its chain length, or 0 if it has not appeared.
narration.7: Appending the current element extends that chain by one.
narration.8: Record the chain ending at this value; a later copy is never worse, so overwriting is safe.
